description: [child row - guidance RESYNCED from parent 2026-09-14; the earlier text here was stale and pointed at a fix that has ALREADY LANDED] DO NOT MODIFY gapClassKey OR ITS REGEX CHAIN. The fix is to make the consumption gate count by LINEAGE, in substrate-gap.ts near the openInClass computation at approximately line 746. Read this paragraph before anything else: two earlier attempts at a regex fix have already been refuted, one by live evidence and one by this substrate's own semantic gate, and a third regex attempt will be refused for the same reason. THE DEFECT. The consumption gate cannot bind on the families that dominate the store, so a compose failure mints children without limit and the lane is eaten by its own failures. MEASURED 2026-09-14: 542 open route-edit rows produce 542 DISTINCT class keys and 398 recommit rows produce 398; across 1,830 open rows there are 1,823 classes and ZERO at or over GAP_CLASS_OPEN_CAP (3). The gate does bind for the detector family it was built for (ids ending in Date.now(), e.g. resolver-dist-orphans and posterior-drift, both sitting at exactly 3), so its logs and unit behaviour look healthy; only a class census over the dominant families reveals it never fires there. WHY THE REGEX ROUTE IS WRONG, TWICE OVER. (1) It is insufficient: this gap's own family now has FOUR members - the parent, a -narrowed child, and two recommit-*-typecheck_dangling_reference children - and NONE of those ids contains an 8-hex token, yet they form four distinct classes. The discriminators there are lane-generated AFFIXES (recommit-/reland- prefixes; -narrowed, -verify_failed, -semantic_reject, -typecheck_dangling_reference, -syntax_break, -anchor_not_found, -compose_execution_failure suffixes), and that list grows every time the lane learns a new failure class, so any enumeration rots. (2) It is hazardous: this substrate's adversarial refuters agreed 2 of 2 (confidence 0.90 and 1.00) that inserting an 8-hex strip after the existing 10-digit and 13-digit epoch strips mis-handles an all-digit 8-character token, because the epoch rules run first and consume digits. That objection is CORRECT and the ordering hazard is inherent to editing this chain. THE FIX - USE DATA THAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND TOUCH NO REGEX. Children already record ancestry: 400 open gaps carry source_gap_id and 201 carry parent_gap_id, together covering 600 of 601 open lane-generated children (99 percent; exactly one lacks a pointer). At the gate, resolve the incoming gap to its LINEAGE ROOT by following parent_gap_id, then source_gap_id, with a depth bound of about 8 and a visited-set so a cycle cannot hang, and count OPEN gaps sharing that root instead of counting gapClassKey matches. Gaps with no pointer are their own root. MEASURED: 1,834 open rows resolve to 1,262 roots with 160 roots at or over 3, versus 29 for the best possible string-surgery rule. It cannot be defeated by a new suffix because it never parses the id. SCOPE - ONE CHANGE. Do not additionally merge independent route-edit roots; under an 8-hex strip that single class would hold 708 open rows and a cap of 3 would refuse essentially every future route-edit filing. That is a separate and far more aggressive policy question, to be decided against a gate that already works. Land lineage capping first, then tune GAP_CLASS_OPEN_CAP as a second, separately measured step.
